'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***Thousands of people flee the northern [[Afghanistan|Afghan]] city of [[Kunduz]] as heavy fighting between [[Afghan National Army|government forces]] and [[Taliban]] [[insurgent]]s nears the city. Heavy clashes are also reported in [[Kandahar Province|Kandahar]] and [[Baghlan Province|Baghlan]] [[provinces of Afghanistan|Provinces]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/27/thousands-displaced-as-government-taliban-fight-near-afghan-city (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]; [[Capital punishment in Somalia]]
**Twenty-one men are [[capital punishment|executed]] by a [[Execution by firing squad|firing squad]] in [[Galkayo]], in the semi-autonomous state of [[Puntland]], [[Somalia]], after they were [[criminal conviction|convicted]] of being members of the [[jihadist]] group [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]]. It is the largest number of executions of members of the group in Puntland. While the executions were being carried out, al-Shabaab gunmen attacked the town of [[Wisil]], [[Mudug]], killing 20 [[Somali Armed Forces|soldiers]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-57630144 (BBC News)]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**Three gun attacks in [[Colombia]] result in multiple deaths. Three off-duty police officers are shot dead in [[Pailitas]], five men are murdered in [[San Vicente del Caguán]], and another officer is killed in [[Cali]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/27/colombia-nine-dead-in-three-separate-attacks-amid-escalating-violence (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir]]
**Two blasts, possibly from [[Unmanned combat aerial vehicle|armed drones]], hit an [[Indian Air Force]] (IAF) base in [[Kashmir|Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir]]. Two IAF personnel suffered minor injuries. The [[Pakistan]]i-based [[Lashkar-e-Taiba]] [[Islamist]] group is believed to be behind the attack. [https://www.dw.com/en/india-explosions-rock-jammu-military-base/a-58063707 (DW)]
*An explosion of a homemade bomb in a church in [[Beni, Democratic Republic of the Congo]],  injures two women. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210627-church-bomb-blast-wounds-two-in-eastern-dr-congo (France 24)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
* Authorities in the [[Turks and Caicos Islands]] said a boat carrying 20 dead individuals, including two children, was discovered drifting approximately a mile off the coast of [[Grand Turk]]. [https://www.klkntv.com/20-people-found-dead-on-boat-drifting-in-turks-and-caicos/ (''AP'')]
* Seven people are killed and dozens are injured in a blast in a building in [[Dhaka]], [[Bangladesh]] and causing damage to seven buildings. The cause of the blast is unknown but it is suspected to be caused by a gas leak. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/police-dead-bangladesh-blast-unknown-78522008 (ABC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] reports a record 119 deaths from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 14,172. [https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/2021/06/27/covid-19-bangladesh-records-highest-daily-death-toll-since-start-of-pandemic (''Dhaka Tribune'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 21,342 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, 9,394 of which are from [[Jakarta]], thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2.11 million. [https://health.detik.com/berita-detikhealth/d-5621986/dki-rekor-9394-kasus-ini-sebaran-21342-kasus-baru-covid-19-ri-27-juni (detikHealth)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine]]
****[[Palestinian Authority|Palestine]] reports its first cases of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant]] in two people from the [[West Bank]] cities of [[Qalqilya]] and [[Salfit]] who recently travelled from the [[United Arab Emirates]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/palestine-confirms-cases-of-delta-strain-of-coronavirus/2286941# (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia]]
****The Saudi Food and Drug Authority approves the inoculation of children between 12 and 17 years of age with the Pfizer–BioNtech COVID-19 vaccine. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/saudi-arabia-inoculate-those-aged-12-18-with-pfizer-vaccine-ministry-2021-06-27/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[Darwin, Northern Territory|Darwin]] and surrounding towns enter a two-day [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] after a [[COVID-19]] outbreak linked to the recent cluster in [[Sydney]] was reported. Restrictions also increase in [[Western Australia]] after a woman who recently returned from Sydney also tests positive. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/jun/27/sydney-covid-cluster-nsw-records-30-new-cases-as-vaccination-hub-identified-as-exposure-site (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Luxembourg]]
***[[Luxembourg]] [[Prime Minister of Luxembourg|Prime Minister]] [[Xavier Bettel]] tests positive for [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.politico.eu/article/luxembourg-xavier-bettel-positive-coronavirus-eu-council-summit/amp/ (Politico.eu)]
*[[2021 Western North America heat wave]]
**The temperature reaches {{convert|46.6|C|F}} in [[Lytton, British Columbia]], breaking the all-time record for hottest temperature ever recorded in Canada. The previous record was {{convert|45|C|F}} in [[Yellow Grass, Saskatchewan|Yellow Grass]] and [[Midale, Saskatchewan]], in 1937. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/b-c-heat-wave-shatters-canadian-record-for-highest-temperature-ever-recorded-1.6082192 (CBC)] 

'''International relations'''
*[[Sudan]] announces that it will surrender former officials who are wanted on [[war crime]] [[criminal charge|charges]] to the [[International Criminal Court]]. Sudan has not named those who will be handed over. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-57628697 (BBC News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Women's rights in Saudi Arabia]]
**[[Saudi Arabia]] releases two [[women's rights]] activists, [[Samar Badawi]] and [[Nassima al-Sadah]], after they completed and served their sentences. Both women were detained in July 2018 along with a dozen other activists. [[Human rights]] group welcome the release, with [[Human Rights Watch]] praising the women's activism. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/saudi-arabia-releases-two-women-activists-says-rights-group-2021-06-27/ (Reuters)]
